name: LND
purpose: Lightning Labs’ Lightning Network node, written in Go: channels, payments, routing and an on-chain wallet, with Bitcoin Core (bitcoind), btcd or Neutrino as its chain backend. It exposes gRPC and REST interfaces authenticated with macaroons, and is the base of Lightning Terminal, Loop and Pool.

maintenance.evidence: v0.21.4-beta and v0.20.5-beta published on 2026-10-01 (two maintained lines); release candidates v0.21.5-beta.rc1 and v0.20.6-beta.rc1 on 2026-10-22; repository pushed on 2026-10-23 and not archived.

platforms.windowsVersions: Not stated by the project. Verified on Windows 10 22H2 (19045) x64 on 2026-10-23.
platforms.windowsDistribution: One ZIP per architecture: lnd-windows-amd64-v0.21.4-beta.zip (49 391 174 bytes), lnd-windows-386 and lnd-windows-arm64, each holding lnd.exe and lncli.exe in a folder of the same name. No installer and no Authenticode signature (both executables reported NotSigned on 2026-10-23). Hashes in manifest-v0.21.4-beta.txt, signed in separate binary OpenPGP files manifest-<signer>-v0.21.4-beta.sig, with OpenTimestamps proofs.
platforms.other: Release archives for other platforms; reproducible builds with go1.27.1 (make release); Docker image lightninglabs/lnd with a /verify-install.sh script.

interfaces.description: REST (grpc-gateway) on restlisten, default localhost:8080: JSON over HTTPS with LND’s self-signed tls.cert. 64-bit integers are strings and bytes are base64. Routes used by BTCortex: /v1/state (answers without a macaroon), /v1/getinfo, /v1/balance/blockchain, /v1/balance/channels, /v1/channels, /v1/channels/pending, /v1/peers, /v1/fees, POST /v1/switch (forwarding history), /v1/invoices, /v1/payments, /v1/graph/info, /v1/channels/backup and /v2/watchtower/client. Streaming calls such as POST /v2/router/send answer with newline-delimited JSON objects {"result": …}.
interfaces.authentication: Macaroon, hex-encoded, in the Grpc-Metadata-macaroon header. Errors are grpc-gateway JSON {code, message, details}; observed on 0.21.4: "expected 1 macaroon, got 0", "verification failed: signature mismatch after caveat verification", "permission denied", "watchtower client not active".

interfaces.description: gRPC on rpclisten, default localhost:10009, with the same certificate and macaroons; used by lncli, Lightning Terminal, Loop and Pool. Sub-servers (routerrpc, walletrpc, invoicesrpc, signrpc, chainrpc, peersrpc, watchtowerrpc and others) are included in release builds.
interfaces.authentication: Macaroon in the macaroon metadata field, TLS with tls.cert.

interfaces.description: Lightning peer protocol (BOLT 8 transport) on listen, default port 9735.
interfaces.authentication: Node keys (Noise_XK).

interfaces.description: lncli.exe drives the gRPC interface.
interfaces.authentication: The same macaroons and certificate.

cli: lnd.exe takes go-flags options; on Windows lnd --help prints the /option:value form and --option=value is also accepted, but a switch takes no value on the command line (--noseedbackup=true is refused, verified on 0.21.4). Exactly one of bitcoin.mainnet, testnet, testnet4, signet, regtest or simnet is required. Settings can also go in lnd.conf, an INI file whose keys carry their namespace (bitcoin.mainnet=true under [Bitcoin]).
remoteManagement: REST and gRPC over TLS with macaroons are meant for remote use: tlsextraip and tlsextradomain add names to the certificate, node packages show lndconnect:// URIs for wallets, and tor.active publishes an onion service. A macaroon can be baked with fewer permissions and with caveats such as time-before.
nodeCompatibility: bitcoin.node=bitcoind needs Bitcoin Core with RPC and either ZMQ (zmqpubrawblock and zmqpubrawtx) or bitcoind.rpcpolling; btcd and Neutrino are the alternatives. Verified on 2026-10-23: LND 0.21.4-beta with Bitcoin Core 31.1 on regtest, using bitcoind.rpccookie and bitcoind.rpcpolling with 1 s polling intervals.

dependencies.notes: Or btcd, or Neutrino without a full node. With bitcoind: RPC credentials or the cookie, and ZMQ or RPC polling.
tor.active for an onion service and for reaching onion peers.

networking: Listens on 9735 for peers, 10009 for gRPC and 8080 for REST (the last two on localhost by default). Connects out to peers, the bitcoind RPC and ZMQ endpoints, and with Tor through its SOCKS port.
storage: Under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lnd: lnd.conf, tls.cert, tls.key, logs, and data\chain\bitcoin\<network>\ with wallet.db, the macaroons (admin, readonly, invoice) and channel.backup; the channel database and graph under data\graph\<network>\ (bbolt by default; SQLite and Postgres backends are compiled into release builds). Mainnet size not measured here.
resources: Not measured on mainnet. On regtest each lnd 0.21.4 process reached synced_to_chain in about 5 s.
security: admin.macaroon can spend; readonly.macaroon is enough for monitoring and can export the static channel backup. tls.cert is self-signed; LND creates a new one when it is deleted, and with tlsautorefresh when its addresses change, which breaks clients that pinned the old one. The wallet is encrypted with the password chosen at creation; the 24-word aezeed seed together with channel.backup recovers channel funds. --noseedbackup creates an unencrypted wallet without showing a seed (tests only). Releases: manifest-v<version>.txt must carry signatures from at least 5 of the 16 keys listed in scripts/verify-install.sh, each user counted once; v0.21.4-beta carried 8 valid signatures (bhandras, boris, georgetsagk, gijswijs, roasbeef, suheb, ViktorT-11, ziggie1984) on 2026-10-23. One listed key (ellemouton) expired on 2026-06-21.
licenceNotes: MIT (LICENSE: Copyright (C) 2015-2022 Lightning Labs and The Lightning Network Developers).
integrationMechanisms: Connect over REST with the read-only macaroon (kept in the vault) and the certificate pinned by its SHA-256 fingerprint
Find LND on this computer in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lnd and read lnd.conf (restlisten, norest, network, datadir, tlscertpath, *macaroonpath) without changing it
Accept lndconnect:// URIs from node packages; refuse the gRPC port 10009
Read what a macaroon allows from its identifier (entity and action pairs) without asking the node
Reach onion addresses through BTCortex’s tor with per-connection SOCKS stream isolation
Export the static channel backup through /v1/channels/backup and keep it in BTCortex’s backups folder
Install the Windows ZIP after checking 5 of the 16 release keys on the manifest (used for integration tests)
Run lnd as a managed process for a BTCortex node (not implemented: creating the wallet shows its seed, which must happen in LND’s own tools)

feasibility.notes: Official Windows builds, documented REST and gRPC, read-only macaroons, and an end-to-end test of BTCortex against three LND 0.21.4 nodes on Windows 10 regtest (payments routed through a middle node, forwarding fees, channel backup verified by LND).

notes: go-flags option syntax and lnd.conf layout were checked against lnd 0.21.4 on Windows. The REST interface reports peer aliases on channels with peer_alias_lookup=true. Gossip of channel policies takes a moment after channels are announced: route queries (/v1/graph/routes) fail until both policies are known.

sources.title: LND config.go at v0.21.4-beta (defaults, networks, TLS options)

unverifiedClaims: Mainnet memory, CPU and disk use were not measured.
Running LND under WSL2 was not tested.
The Docker image’s verification script was not tried.

name: Core Lightning
purpose: Blockstream’s Lightning implementation in C with a plugin architecture; JSON-RPC over a Unix socket, with gRPC (cln-grpc) and REST (clnrest) plugins authenticated by runes.

maintenance.evidence: v26.06.9 published on 2026-10-07; repository pushed on 2026-10-22 and not archived.

platforms.other: Release binaries for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 (amd64, arm64, armv7) and Fedora 40 (amd64), with SHA256SUMS signed in SHA256SUMS-v26.06.9.asc; build instructions for Ubuntu, Fedora, NixOS and macOS; Docker image elementsproject/lightningd. The installation guide mentions no Windows.

interfaces.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the lightning-rpc Unix socket in the network directory; lightning-cli uses it.
interfaces.authentication: Access to the socket file.

interfaces.description: clnrest plugin: enabled by clnrest-port (3010 is common; the plugin disables itself without it), HTTPS by default (clnrest-protocol), on 127.0.0.1 by default (clnrest-host), certificates from clnrest-certs (by default the gRPC ones). Every RPC method is POST /v1/<method>; a Swagger interface and a Socket.IO notification stream are served on the same port.
interfaces.authentication: A rune in the Rune header (createrune, showrunes); a read-only rune suffices for read methods and for notifications.

interfaces.description: cln-grpc plugin on grpc-port with mutual TLS.
interfaces.authentication: Client certificates generated by the plugin.

cli: lightningd and lightning-cli (JSON-RPC over the Unix socket).
remoteManagement: clnrest (HTTPS with runes) or cln-grpc (mutual TLS) for remote clients; node packages expose them.
nodeCompatibility: Bitcoin Core through the bcli plugin (bitcoin-cli), so a reachable bitcoind with RPC is required.
networking: Peers on 9735; clnrest and cln-grpc only when their ports are set.
security: Runes carry restrictions (methods, parameters, rate, expiry) and can be revoked. Release checksums are signed (SHA256SUMS-<version>.asc).
licenceNotes: LICENSE: the ccan/ modules have their own licences; the rest is under the BSD-MIT licence.
integrationMechanisms: Remote connection through clnrest with a read-only rune (not implemented)
WSL2 or Docker deployment (not implemented)

feasibility.notes: No Windows build, so only a remote connection (clnrest) or WSL2/Docker is possible; clnrest is a straightforward HTTPS JSON interface, but no Windows test environment exists here to verify it against a real node.

notes: Never claim that Core Lightning runs natively on Windows.
unverifiedClaims: WSL2 operation not tested.
The gRPC documentation page was not read (docs.corelightning.org refused automated access); the description follows the repository.

name: Eclair
purpose: ACINQ’s Lightning implementation in Scala on the JVM, built for large routing nodes; it uses Bitcoin Core’s wallet for on-chain funds and offers an HTTP JSON API.

maintenance.evidence: v0.14.5 published on 2026-10-20; repository pushed on 2026-10-22 and not archived.

platforms.windowsDistribution: eclair-node-0.14.5-01384e9-bin.zip, a JVM distribution, with SHA256SUMS.asc. Eclair targets Java 21 and "will run on any compatible Java runtime"; Windows is not mentioned.
platforms.other: Any platform with a Java 21 runtime.

interfaces.description: HTTP API (eclair.api.enabled, off by default) on eclair.api.port, default 8080; must not be reachable from outside.
interfaces.authentication: HTTP Basic with eclair.api.password (required when the API is on).

interfaces.description: Lightning peers on eclair.server.port, default 9735.

cli: eclair-cli (a shell script over the API).
remoteManagement: The HTTP API with its password, through a secure tunnel.
nodeCompatibility: Bitcoin Core 31 or later, synchronised, with ZMQ (zmqpubhashblock, zmqpubrawtx), its wallet enabled, txindex and no pruning; channel funding and closing use the Bitcoin Core wallet, which must be backed up.

dependencies.notes: Bitcoin Core 31+, wallet enabled, ZMQ, txindex=1, not pruned.

networking: 9735 for peers; API on 8080 when enabled. Remote bitcoind only through an encrypted tunnel (the project’s own warning).
security: The API gives full control and must stay private; funds are in the Bitcoin Core wallet as well as in channels.
integrationMechanisms: Connect to the HTTP API with its password (not implemented)

feasibility.notes: A JVM application could run on Windows, but its requirements on Bitcoin Core (wallet, ZMQ, txindex) and Java 21 make it an operator’s tool; Windows operation is not documented.

unverifiedClaims: Running Eclair on Windows was not tested.
The Docker image status is from memory of community images and was not checked.

name: The Eye of Satoshi (teos)
purpose: Lightning watchtower compliant with BOLT 13, which watches the chain for breaches of its users’ channels; its client is a Core Lightning plugin (watchtower-client).

maintenance.evidence: The latest release is v0.2.0 from 2023-02-07; the repository was last pushed on 2025-10-09.

platforms.other: Built from source; the release has no binaries.

interfaces.description: The tower’s API for its clients (defaults in teos/src/config.rs), optionally as an onion service with --torsupport.

cli: teosd (the tower); --torsupport needs a Tor daemon on the same machine with its control port open.
nodeCompatibility: Clients: the watchtower-client plugin for Core Lightning; the README names no LND client.
security: No release since 2023. A tower that fails to react cannot stop a peer from publishing an old channel state, so an unmaintained tower is a weak safeguard; with --torsupport it needs the control port of a local Tor daemon.

feasibility.notes: No release since 2023 and no Windows builds; LND has a watchtower of its own.

unverifiedClaims: Default ports, its node requirements and supported operating systems were not examined.

name: Breez SDK
purpose: Library for adding non-custodial bitcoin and stablecoin payments to applications without running a node, over Lightning and Spark with on-chain interoperability, with bindings for Kotlin, Swift, JavaScript, React Native, Flutter, Go, Python, C# and WebAssembly.

maintenance.evidence: Breez SDK Spark 0.27.2 published on 2026-10-23.

platforms.other: Bindings for application developers.

interfaces.description: SDK API in its supported languages.
interfaces.authentication: A Breez API key, free, requested from Breez.

nodeCompatibility: Nodeless: it does not use the user’s node.
security: Non-custodial: its documentation says users can always withdraw to the Bitcoin blockchain without the Spark operators (unilateral exit). Applications need an API key from Breez.

feasibility.notes: An SDK for building payment applications; nothing for BTCortex to install or connect to.

notes: sdk-doc.breez.technology now redirects to the Spark SDK’s documentation; the earlier Greenlight-based and Liquid-based variants were not examined.
unverifiedClaims: How the earlier Breez SDK variants relate to the Spark SDK (superseded or still maintained) was not checked.

name: Greenlight
purpose: Blockstream’s service of hosted, non-custodial Lightning nodes (Core Lightning, “the c-lightning instance” in its README) for developers and their users, controlled over gRPC while the seed stays on the user’s device.

maintenance.evidence: The repository (client libraries and tools) was pushed on 2026-10-21.

platforms.other: A hosted service with client libraries; gl-cli on crates.io.

interfaces.description: The scheduler and each node are reached over gRPC with mutual TLS.
interfaces.authentication: A developer certificate (client.crt and client-key.pem, downloaded from the Greenlight Developer Console) authenticates the application to the scheduler and allows registering nodes.

nodeCompatibility: Hosted nodes; not the user’s own node.
security: The seed must be kept on the user’s device and never on an application server; the node itself runs on Blockstream’s infrastructure.
licenceNotes: The licence covers the repository (client libraries and tools); the service is operated by Blockstream.

feasibility.notes: A developer service for embedding hosted nodes in applications; nothing for a Windows user to install, and a hosted node is not the user’s own.

unverifiedClaims: How client devices authenticate to their own nodes was not examined.

name: ZEUS
purpose: Mobile Bitcoin and Lightning wallet and remote node manager for LND and Core Lightning on Android and iOS, which can also run an embedded node (LND or LDK Node).

maintenance.evidence: v13.2.3 published on 2026-10-12, with a signed manifest.

platforms.other: Android (zeus-v13.2.3-arm64-v8a.apk, zeus-v13.2.3-universal.apk) and iOS (zeus-v13.2.3.ipa), with manifest-v13.2.3.txt and its signature.

interfaces.description: Connects to a remote LND or Core Lightning node, LNDHub instances and Lightning Node Connect, optionally over Tor; Nostr Wallet Connect as a service and as a client.
interfaces.authentication: The node’s own credentials (for example an LND macaroon).

remoteManagement: It is itself a remote manager for LND and Core Lightning nodes.
nodeCompatibility: Remote LND and Core Lightning; 13.2.3 embeds LND 0.21.4 and LDK Node 0.7.0 with rust-lightning 0.2.7.

dependencies.notes: For remote-node mode; it can also run an embedded node.

networking: Outbound connections from the phone to the node, directly, over Tor or through Lightning Node Connect.
security: A remote connection gives the phone the node’s credentials, so a limited macaroon limits what a lost phone can do. 13.2.3 adds further security hardening and rust-lightning 0.2.7’s security fixes.
licenceNotes: The commercial fonts in assets/fonts and android/app/src/main/assets/fonts are not covered by the AGPL.
integrationMechanisms: Show the user’s LND connection details as an lndconnect address or QR code for ZEUS to scan (not built)

feasibility.notes: BTCortex could hand ZEUS a connection to the user’s LND (a QR code with a limited macaroon, reachable over Tor), but it does not export LND credentials yet.

unverifiedClaims: The signing key of the release manifest was not identified.

name: chantools
purpose: Rescue tool for funds locked in LND channels when LND itself cannot run properly, for example zombie channels or channels force-closed by the peer; some commands also support Core Lightning.

platforms.windowsDistribution: ZIP archive chantools-windows-amd64-v0.14.3.zip, with manifest-v0.14.3.txt and its signature
platforms.other: Linux (386, amd64, arm64, armv6, armv7) and macOS (amd64, arm64) archives.

interfaces.description: Commands such as summary, rescueclosed, sweepremoteclosed, zombierecovery, triggerforceclose, sweeptimelock, forceclose and compactdb.
interfaces.authentication: Many commands need the wallet seed, typed in the terminal, or a root key or environment variable.

cli: chantools; --apiurl points the commands that query a block explorer at the user’s own.
nodeCompatibility: Works on LND’s channel.db and seed; summary, compactdb and dumpchannels need no seed; zombierecovery also works with Core Lightning.

dependencies.notes: Its data (channel.db) and, for many commands, its seed.

networking: Some commands query public block explorer APIs unless --apiurl is given.
security: Many commands need the wallet seed; the README says it never leaves the computer and that typing it in the terminal is the safest way. Some commands query public block explorers, which costs privacy. forceclose publishes an old channel state and is only for peers that are gone for good. The README warns that it was built for particular rescue operations and should be reviewed before serious use.

feasibility.notes: Its rescue commands need the wallet seed, and BTCortex never asks for or handles seeds; its documentation can point users to chantools for rescues outside BTCortex.

unverifiedClaims: The signing key of the release manifest was not identified.
